## Exercise 0.1: Draw the chain for one file {#ex-0.1}

Working backward from `peaks/HCT116_CTCF_1_peaks.narrowPeak`, reading the
scripts in `snakemakeify/`:

```text
peaks/HCT116_CTCF_1_peaks.narrowPeak                       04_call_peaks.sh
├── HCT116_CTCF_1.filt.bam                                 03_filter.sh
│   └── HCT116_CTCF_1.bam                                  02_align.sh
│       ├── data/fastq/HCT116_CTCF_1.fastq.gz              (raw data)
│       └── chr8_course.*.bt2                              02_align.sh (index)
│           └── chr8_course.fa                             02_align.sh (gunzip)
│               └── data/reference/chr8_course.fa.gz       (raw data)
├── HCT116_input-CTCF_1.filt.bam                           03_filter.sh
│   └── HCT116_input-CTCF_1.bam                            02_align.sh
│       ├── data/fastq/HCT116_input-CTCF_1.fastq.gz        (raw data)
│       └── chr8_course.*.bt2                              (same index as above)
└── data/samplesheet.txt                                   (says which control)
```

Two things are easy to miss. The control BAM is an input, because
`04_call_peaks.sh` passes `-c $control.filt.bam` to MACS3. And the samplesheet
is an input too: change the `Control` column and the right answer changes,
even though no BAM did.

Now delete `HCT116_input-CTCF_1.bam` and run `run_all.sh`. Step 02 makes a
new BAM for that sample. After that, three files in the drawing are out of
date:

- `HCT116_input-CTCF_1.filt.bam` (made from the old BAM),
- `peaks/HCT116_CTCF_1_peaks.narrowPeak` (used the old control),
- and, outside the drawing, `tracks/HCT116_input-CTCF_1.bw`, which
  `03_filter.sh` makes from the same filtered BAM.

`run_all.sh` remakes **none** of them. Step 03 sees
`HCT116_input-CTCF_1.filt.bam` exists and skips; step 04 sees the peak file
exists and skips. To get correct results you must know the chain above and
delete the three files yourself.

In Snakemake, the new BAM is newer than the filtered BAM made from it, so the
filter job reruns, and that makes the peak job's input newer, so it reruns as
well. You get the same result without having to draw anything. That is the
whole argument of module 0, and module 1 starts building it.
